title: A FEAST OF JOY AND ABUNDANCE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. Celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days. Present as an aroma pleasing to the LORD a food offering consisting of a burnt offering of thirteen young bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect." - Num 29:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Five days after the solemn Day of Atonement came the Festival of Tabernacles, a seven-day celebration of great joy. This feast, marked by the largest number of offerings in the whole calendar, was a time of thanksgiving and gladness. Having been reconciled through atonement, the people now rejoiced abundantly before their God.

There is a beautiful order here. Solemn atonement came first, and then overflowing joy. This is always the pattern of grace. When our sin has been dealt with and we are reconciled to God, the natural fruit is deep and abundant joy. Forgiveness leads to celebration. The heart set free from guilt overflows with gladness.

During this feast, Israel lived in temporary shelters to remember how God had cared for them in the wilderness. It was a festival of remembering God's faithful provision throughout their journey. They looked back on all the ways He had sustained them and gave thanks with joyful hearts.

For those in Christ, the sequence is the same: atonement first, then joy. Because Jesus has reconciled us to God, we can celebrate with a gladness that nothing can take away. Indeed, Jesus taught during this very feast, offering living water to all who are thirsty (John 7:37-38). Come to Him, remember His faithful provision, and let your reconciled heart overflow with joy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the joy of forgiveness overflow in your life?
2. How does remembering God's faithful provision stir gratitude in you?
3. What does it mean to celebrate with a joy nothing can take away?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that atonement leads to abundant joy. Because Christ has reconciled me to You, help my heart overflow with gladness as I remember Your faithful provision all my days. Amen.
